newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians call for strike over Israel tax raids.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians call for strike over Israel tax raids.

text.p: Palestinian businesses in Arab East Jerusalem will shut down in a general strike next week in protest at Israeli tax raids, an East Jerusalem Chamber of Commerce official said on Friday.

"We have called for a full strike on Sunday. All businesses in East Jerusalem will be closed over Israeli tax raids directed against Palestinians," Ziyyad Hamouri, a member of a Palestinian ad-hoc anti-tax action committee, told Reuters.
Israel in June launched a tax raid campaign in Jerusalem.

The strike marks an escalation in what Palestinians say is Israeli economic warfare to drive them out of East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed in a move not recognised by the international community.
The Israeli municipality of Jerusalem says raids are conducted in both East Jerusalem and Jewish West Jerusalem and denies they are politically motivated.
"This is a warning strike. It is one of several steps," Hamouri said.
Arab merchants this week held a one-hour strike and demonstrated in downtown East Jerusalem's commercial heart.
Hamouri said Palestinian small businesses -- some defunct for years -- have been ordered to pay taxes in excess of their business capital.
Palestinians complain they receive fewer and poorer services for taxes collected by the municipality.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state. Israel says it will not cede sovereignty over any part of the city it claims as its unified capital.
